name: label
title: Label
description: An accessible name for a form control, with no state of its own.
docs:
## When to use - Every input, textarea, select, checkbox, radio, switch, and slider that needs a visible name. - A group of controls that share one caption. - A field whose purpose is not obvious from the placeholder alone (which is almost every field). ## When not to use - As a placeholder. A placeholder disappears on the first keystroke and is not a name; use a real `Label`. - As a heading. If the text introduces a section, use a heading so it appears in the document outline. - For helper text or error text; those belong in the description/error slot so they can be wired through `aria-describedby`. ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/label ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Input } from "@/components/cadence/input/input"; import { Label } from "@/components/cadence/label/label"; export function EmailField() { return (
); } ``` ## Examples ### Wrapping instead of `htmlFor` Either association works: `htmlFor` + `id`, or wrapping the control. Pick one per field and keep it consistent. ```tsx ``` ### Disabled The label follows the control without any prop: `peer-disabled:` handles a sibling control, `group-data-[disabled=true]:` handles a disabled `Field`. ```tsx ``` ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | ----------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------ | | `htmlFor` | `string` | – | Id of the control this label names. | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last. | All native `label` props are forwarded. ## Motion contract No motion (T0).
